facility.name: Kerrville's Bright Beginnings
facility.programs_provided: School Age Care,Meals Provided ,After School Care,Snacks Provided,Part Time Care,Transportation to/from School ,Field Trips

provenance.note: Census Geocoder Exact match: 551 MEADOWVIEW LN, KERRVILLE, TX, 78028

inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age: The operation scheduled one caregiver for the first 30 minutes of operating hours to accept and care for infants-4 year olds. All children met in the 2-3 year old classroom.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: An outlet cover in the school-age room was opened at a 90 degree angle creating a hazard resulting in a child hitting their head on the cover requiring medical treatment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Care Requirements for School-age - Caregiver Aware of Arrival/Departure: The operation failed to use their attendance taking system when children arrived from public school and were not aware that a school-age child did not get off the public school bus at the operation.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Care Requirements for School-age - Caregiver Aware of Arrival/Departure (26 TAC §746.2701(4))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: The training certificate that was provided for the caregiver who provided first aid at the time of the accident did not meet the requirements for first aid certification.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization: The operation failed to report to Child Care Regulation that a child had received medical treatment after an injury occurred while the child was in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Report Child Injury Requiring Medical Treatment by a Health-Care Professional or Hospitalization (26 TAC §746.305(a)(2))

occurrences.finding: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent: The operation failed to provide incident/illness report 7239 to the parent or obtain parent signature on an initial injury report after a child received an injury while in care.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Incident/Illness Report Form Shared with Parent (26 TAC §746.707)

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: During the course of the investigation, it was determined that the school-age classroom utilized screen time during nap time during the summer.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Exceed One Hour Daily: During the course of the investigation, it was determined that the school-age room has screen time for up to four hours on one day and one and a half hours on another day during the summer.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Exceed One Hour Daily (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(3))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact: Seven out of 10 child files evaluated were missing or had incomplete emergency contact addresses.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Emergency Contact (26 TAC §746.605(6))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards: There is a protruding circular piece of metal in the rock area of the older playground and a covered water pipe full of water in a portion of the playground where children have to pass through to get to the back playground.  Children can lift the lid and have access to the standing water.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Areas Free From Hazards (26 TAC §746.3701)

occurrences.finding: Active Play Surfacing In Use Zones - Loose Fill or Unitary Surfacing: The loose fill around the two playscapes and under the swing set is less than an inch in depth or not evident at the end of the slides.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Active Play Surfacing In Use Zones - Loose Fill or Unitary Surfacing (26 TAC §746.4901(a))

occurrences.finding: Required Admission Information - Date of Admission: There were two out of ten child files evaluated missing their enrollment start date.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Date of Admission (26 TAC §746.605(3))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Sprinkler Play - Equipment and Water Hoses Kept Out of Child's Reach: A water hose attached to the faucet off the infant back door had not been secured.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Sprinkler Play - Equipment and Water Hoses Kept Out of Child's Reach (26 TAC §746.5015(c))

occurrences.finding: Health Statement on File within 1 Week of Admission: One out of ten child files evaluated was missing a health statement upon enrollment in October.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Health Statement on File within 1 Week of Admission (26 TAC §746.611(b))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Two out of ten child files evaluated did not contain a copy of the child's vaccination records.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Records - Immunizations (26 TAC §746.603(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking.: During the investigation, it was found that a caregiver who had unsupervised access to children did not have first aid certification.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Each Caregiver and the Director Must Have Current Training in pediatric first aid with rescue breathing and choking. (26 TAC §746.1315(a))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children: A caregiver was observed pulling a child by the leg twice while they were sitting outside to bring the child closer to the caregiver.  The second time, the child fell backwards, hitting their head on the ground.  The same caregiver was observed pulling a child by their clothing and pushing them away from an object while on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Interact positively with children (26 TAC §746.1203(5))

occurrences.finding: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control: A caregiver used poor judgment when they pushed an infant's head onto a mat they were laying on outside and began rubbing the side of the infant's head on the mat in order to clean their face after the infant spit up.  The same caregiver was later observed picking up a child by one arm and carrying them upside down to return them to their cot during naptime.  A second caregiver was observed carrying a child right below their wrists to another caregiver while on the playground.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Responsibilities of Employees and Caregivers -Demonstrate Competency, Good Judgment, Self-control (26 TAC §746.1201(1))

occurrences.finding: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep: During the investigation, a caregiver reported putting a book on a child's back during naptime to create the feeling of a weight to put the child to sleep.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children Not Required to Sleep - May Not Force Child to Sleep (26 TAC §746.2905(1))

occurrences.finding: Annual Sanitation Inspection: The last Health Inspection was conducted on 11/6/2024.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Annual Sanitation Inspection (26 TAC §746.3401(a))

occurrences.finding: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation: A caregiver relieved another caregiver in the infant room for break and did not have an eligibility letter on file.    NOTE: The caregiver was sent home and a background check request was entered during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)

occurrences.finding: Measurement of Use Zone for Stationary Equipment: On the older playground, there was a balance beam and a bench within 3 ft of eachother.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Measurement of Use Zone for Stationary Equipment (26 TAC §746.4803)

occurrences.finding: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children: Three classroom restrooms had mop buckets and water accessible to the children.  Classrooms use soap and water buckets to clean table tops.  Spray bottles were accessible in the restroom to children in the prek room. There was a toilet brush laying on top of the toilet lid in the 2 yr room.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Mark Cleaning Supplies, Toxic Materials; Keep Separate from Food and Inaccessible to Children (26 TAC §746.3407(12))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - Anchoring devices Below Level of Playing Surface: There wre three metal, stationary riding toys anchored to the ground that had the metal base exposed.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Active Play Equipment - Anchoring devices Below Level of Playing Surface (26 TAC §746.4601(6))

occurrences.finding: Safety - Play Materials and Equipment Safe: The red climber on the 2 yr old playground had peeling paint. One blue boat on the prek playground had broken boards.  There were two carpets in the school-age room that were curling on the edges.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety - Play Materials and Equipment Safe (26 TAC §746.3701(5))

occurrences.finding: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner: Two trash cans in the prek room restrooms, one in the toddler room restroom, and one outside of the gym restrooms did not have a lid.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Garbage Inaccessible to Children; Maintained in Sanitary Manner (26 TAC §746.3407(8))

occurrences.finding: Animals at Center - Statement of Health from Veterinarian: There wasn't a health statement on file for the pet guinea pig in the Kinder-ready room.    NOTE:  The caregiver took the guinea pig home during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Animals at Center - Statement of Health from Veterinarian (26 TAC §746.3903(b))
